messages:
Maya: Quick ask — can we add a tiny 'fallback to cheaper-variant' example to the Dedicated provisioning docs? Customers keep asking how Dedicated falls back to lower-tier models during surge and what that means for SLA/isolation. cc @kevin @liam

Kevin: +1. I can draft a minimal YAML showing scalePolicy with fallbackModel and a short note about SLA impact.

Liam: Also call out tenant isolation labels and preemption behavior. Support had a ticket about billing and rate limits when fallback kicks in.

docs-bot: Draft PR created: (draft) https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/0000 — add snippets below to the PR description.

Maya: Copying proposed snippets here so we can iterate quickly. Keep comments inline.

Kevin: YAML snippet (minimal, for the provisioning guide):
```yaml
provisioning:
  tenant: acme-corp
  reserved_capacity:
    gpus: 4
    model: rdl-large-v1
  scalePolicy:
    target_qps: 120
    cooldown_s: 90
    fallbackModel: rdl-medium-quantized-v1  # cheaper variant used when capacity constrained
    fallback_policy:
      max_fallback_pct: 40  # at most 40% of traffic can be routed to fallback
  tenant_labels:
    isolation: high
```

Kevin: Notes: - When fallbackModel is used, per-request latency might change and unit cost decreases. - For reserved customers, committed throughput is preserved; fallback is for best-effort overflow.

Liam: SDK example (Python) to request routing that accepts fallback:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
resp = client.generate(
    model="rdl-large-v1",
    prompt="Summarize sales deck",
    routing_preferences={
        "allow_fallback": True,
        "preferred_regions": ["us-west-2"]
    },
    tenant_labels={"isolation": "high"}
)
print(resp.text)
```

sre-jen: two quick ops notes: (1) add a one-liner that fallback does NOT reduce reserved SLA commitments for contracted Dedicated customers (it only applies to burst/overflow). (2) clarify that regional failover policies can override fallback behavior — mention cross-region canary/rollout implications.

Kevin: Updated PR text to include SLA one-liner and a short link to SLA page: https://redwood.example/sla (internal).

Liam: LGTM on wording. One more ask: can we include a tiny troubleshooting bullet for "why did my tenant get partially routed to fallback?" — mention quota vs. reserved limits.

Maya: Good call — I'll add that bullet. For this PR let's ship the YAML + SDK + two short notes (SLA and troubleshooting). I'll add a follow-up with a small traffic-sim harness for the examples. :shipit:

docs-bot: PR updated with snippets and notes. Reviewers requested: @kevin @liam @sre-jen

Kevin: I'll review today and merge if no blockers.

Liam: Thanks — will watch for the follow-up harness.

Maya: Thanks all!
